extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and NIH peer reviewers (SROs, study section members, IC staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for initial (SRG) and second-level (Advisory Council/Board) peer review of NIH research grant and cooperative agreement applications, including roles, scored criteria, additional considerations, scoring procedures, and post-review actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The core values of peer review drive the NIH to seek the highest level of ethical standards and form the foundation for laws, regulations, and policies that govern NIH peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH policy is intended to promote a process whereby grant applications are evaluated on a process that strives to be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual peer review system (first and second level)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a dual peer review system mandated by statute: an initial review by a Scientific Review Group (SRG) and a second level of review by Institute/Center Advisory Councils or Boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by the IC Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SRG is led by an SRO, an NIH extramural staff scientist and the designated federal official responsible for ensuring objective and fair initial peer review and compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs analyze application content and completeness; document and manage conflicts of interest; recruit qualified reviewers; assign applications to reviewers for critique preparation and assignment of individual criterion scores; attend and oversee administrative and regulatory aspects of meetings; and prepare summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: SROs recruit qualified reviewers based on scientific and technical qualifications and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include authority in their scientific field, dedication to high quality/fair/objective reviews, ability to work collegially in a group setting, experience in research grant review, and balanced representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG Chair role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair serves as moderator of the discussion of scientific and technical merit and also serves as a peer reviewer for the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair organizes and moderates discussion and participates in scoring as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities (conflict of interest, confidentiality, critique, scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest, maintain confidentiality, prepare written critiques, assign numerical scores to scored review criteria, and make recommendations concerning scientific and technical merit and other applicable protections or budget appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers receive access to applications ~six weeks prior to the meeting, must follow 'Managing Conflict of Interest in NIH Peer Review' guidance, use Review Critique Templates as directed by the SRO, and make recommendations concerning human subjects protections, inclusion, vertebrate animal welfare, biohazards, and budget appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other NIH staff attendance and input
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal officials with need-to-know or pertinent responsibilities may attend closed review meetings; NIH IC or other federal staff wishing to attend must have advance approval from the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These individuals may provide programmatic or grants management input at the SRO's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant conduct during the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must maintain the integrity of the peer review process by not contacting reviewers to influence the outcome, not sending information directly to a reviewer, and not accessing information related to the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are consequences for violating confidentiality or attempting to influence reviewers (see Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact is assessed in consideration of the scored review criteria and applicable additional review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers give a separate score for this criterion (see Scoring). Scores for scored criteria (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) are reported to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the scored review criteria; evaluates the investigators involved in the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers provide a numerical score for this criterion and discuss its contribution to overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the scored review criteria; evaluates the novelty of concepts, approaches, or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers score Innovation separately and consider it in the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the scored review criteria; evaluates the strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach is scored separately; reviewers judge rigor and feasibility and that score factors into the overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the scored review criteria; evaluates the institutional support, resources, and environment for successful completion of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment is scored separately and contributes to the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion that reviewers evaluate as applicable, but for which no separate score is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered while determining scientific and technical merit and in providing an overall impact score as applicable for the project proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion evaluated as applicable without a separate numeric score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider inclusion plans when determining overall scientific/technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion addressing vertebrate animal welfare considered as applicable without separate scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will evaluate vertebrate animal protections and consider these in the overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion regarding biohazardous materials and safety, evaluated as applicable without separate scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biohazard concerns are considered in determining scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion considered for revised/resubmitted applications, evaluated as applicable without a separate score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will consider resubmission history and responses to prior review when making merit assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion applicable to renewal (competing continuation) applications, considered without a separate score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess progress and justification for continued support when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional review criterion for revisions of currently funded projects, considered without separate scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions are considered for their scientific rationale and impact on the overall project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: An item reviewers should consider as applicable but should not give a separate score or include in overall impact scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Additional Review Considerations; may affect programmatic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should consider select agent involvement as an additional consideration (not separately scored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of safety/regulatory considerations that should not be used to compute the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of resource sharing (data, model organisms, etc.) that reviewers should consider but not score separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource sharing plans are evaluated as appropriate but are not to be included in the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of plans to authenticate key resources relevant to the proposed research, evaluated as an additional consideration without separate scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentication plans may affect feasibility and reproducibility assessments but are not scored separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and proposed project period are considerations that reviewers should consider but should not score or include in overall impact scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may comment on appropriateness of budget requests; program staff handle programmatic/budget decisions later.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH scoring system and procedures (9-point rating scale and score calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; same scale used for overall impact and criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the SRG meeting each assigned reviewer gives separate scores for each of the (at least) five review criteria and a preliminary overall impact score. For discussed applications, eligible committee members give a final impact score; the final overall impact score is the mean of final impact scores multiplied by 10, yielding scores from 10 (high impact) through 90 (low impact). Applications not discussed receive ND (may be reported as ++).

rubrics_metrics.name: ND designation (Not Discussed) and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that are not discussed at the meeting will be designated 'ND' (may be reported as ++ on the face page) and do not receive numerical impact scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers' written comments and criterion scores are still provided to the applicant and NIH staff as feedback on the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRFC designation (Not Recommended for Further Consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated NRFC by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit or presents serious ethical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRFC grounds include lack of significant merit or serious ethical problems in human subjects protection, vertebrate animal use, biohazards, and/or select agents; NRFC applications do not proceed to the second level of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement and Percentile reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements include written comments and scores; percentiles indicate the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a subset of applications receive percentiles; percentiles are reported as whole numbers; the summary statement will identify the base used to determine the percentile. For ad hoc sections a different base may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process and allowable grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has an appeals system to seek reconsideration of initial review results if applicants believe the review process was flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed grounds: bias of a reviewer, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the review outcome. Policy does not apply to appeals of technical evaluation of R&D contract projects, appeals of NIH funding decisions, or appeals of MERIT award extension decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review by Advisory Council/Board (recommendation process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards perform the second level of review; members are scientists and public representatives chosen by the IC and approved by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff examine applications and consider overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), and summary statements in light of the IC's priorities, provide a grant-funding plan to the council, and council members have access to applications and summary statements pending funding. The Advisory Council advises the IC director, who makes final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Council Review for highly funded investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members conduct a Special Council Review of grant applications from investigators who currently receive $1 million or more in direct costs of NIH funding to support Research Project Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review determines if additional funds should be provided to already well-supported investigators and does not represent a cap on NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review options for not-funded applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is not funded, applicants may resubmit with changes addressing reviewer concerns or submit a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving a summary statement are directed to 'Next Steps' information and may contact the NIH Program Official listed on the summary statement for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundable score considerations and paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs publish paylines as part of funding strategies to guide applicants on likelihood of receiving funding; application scores are compared against the payline for the fiscal year when the application will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paylines may be delayed at fiscal year start; if an IC does not announce a payline, the program official may provide guidance. After award, program officials and grants management staff handle scientific/programmatic and budgetary/administrative matters respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Review Critique Templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must prepare written critiques using Review Critique Templates as directed by the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates standardize written feedback and ensure critiques address review criteria and considerations identified in the FOA.
